name: inputs-pane-rebinds-a-shortcut
description:
A chord rebound in the Inputs pane acts, and the chord it replaced does not - no relaunch. renderInputs used to be a viewer: a settings-row-value span with no control and no chrome.send anywhere in the function, and NativeHotkeyMap::SetFromJSON had exactly one caller (SeedFromSettings at startup), so a hand-edited hotkeys.json only took effect on the next launch. The pane now carries a Record and a Clear button per row, and AtriumSettingsWindow::OnHotkeysSaved calls SetFromJSON on every successful write, which is the live-reload half.

toggleSidebar is the action under test for the same reason hotkey-rebind picked it: its stock-key release is the only effect observable without a second window, and a sibling scenario already measured the pixel deltas this scenario reuses. The fixture stages cmd+s, the stock combo, so the Clear leg has something real to remove rather than clearing an already-empty row.

THE REBIND IS TWO WRITES, Clear then Record, not one 'replace' - the pane has no replace control, only Add-a-combo and Clear-the-row. Clearing first is also what makes the old chord's cmd+s leg land on Save Page afterwards, exactly as a sibling scenario's own notes explain: releasing the stock combo sets sidebar_toggle_combo_bound=false in AtriumCommandInterceptInputs, so IDC_SAVE_PAGE runs for real and a native Save As sheet needs the same double-Escape dismissal a sibling scenario and savepage-swallow both use.

THE CAPTURE CONTROL IS DRIVEN BY A REAL KEY EVENT, not eval. Record puts a document-level, capture-phase keydown listener in the Settings window; at the moment cmd+shift+j is pressed nothing has bound that combo yet, so NativeHotkeyMap has nothing to intercept and the native keydown reaches the WebContents as an ordinary DOM event, which is what comboFromKeydown reads. Everything before and after that one key action is eval, the same split routing-pane-adds-a-rule.json uses for its own pane-then-navigation proof.
